rgeodesy: an R interface to Rust Geodesy

Source: R/geod.R
rgeodesy-package.Rd

rgeodesy exposes the Rust Geodesy (RG) library by Thomas Knudsen — a platform for experiments with geodetic transformations and data flow. You build a transformation by writing a pipeline string of named operators and apply it to vectors of coordinates.

Specifying a transformation

Rust Geodesy does not use EPSG codes or "from" -> "to" CRS pairs. Instead you describe the transformation directly as a pipeline of operator primitives, separated by |, each with key=value arguments:

gis:in | utm zone=32 | gis:out

Coordinates are handled in RG's internal convention (radians, geographic latitude-first), so geographic input/output is wrapped with an adaptor:

  • gis:in / gis:out take degrees in the GIS order (longitude, latitude) — i.e. the natural (x, y) order, recommended for most R users.

  • geo:in / geo:out take degrees in the geodetic order (latitude, longitude).

Operator families (Rust Geodesy 0.15)

  • Projections: utm, tmerc, btmerc/butm (Bowring series), merc, webmerc, lcc, laea, omerc, somerc.

  • Datum / reference-frame transforms: cart, helmert, molodensky, gridshift, deformation.

  • Geodetic computations: geodesic, curvature, gravity, latitude, deflection, permtide.

  • Adaptors and units: adapt, axisswap, unitconvert, dm, dms, the geo:* / gis:* / neu:* / enu:* I/O macros, and noop.

Call geod_ops() for the full list and geod_validate() to check a pipeline before using it. See the operator documentation for arguments.
